executive_summary: Ather’s September result marks positive operating profit before other income, helped by volume, pricing and software attachment. The reported PAT is only ₹1.26 crore and relies on other income to bridge depreciation and interest; capacity expansion and sustainable vehicle economics remain the investment questions.
research_stance: An operating inflection with meaningful execution risk; one small PAT profit is not a mature earnings base.
results_analysis: The local consolidated September quarter records revenue ₹1,464.24 crore, operating profit ₹11.46 crore and PAT ₹1.26 crore. Revenue grew 62.9% year-on-year and 20.3% sequentially. Earlier losses make percentage PAT growth misleading; the transition is assessed in rupees.

Operating profit changed not meaningful on a loss/zero base YoY and not meaningful on a loss/zero base QoQ. The calculated operating-profit/sales margin is 0.78%, versus -14.75% a year earlier and -2.73% in June. These calculations use a consistently rounded local series; management EBITDA may use a different scope or definition.

Local operating profit of ₹11.46 crore equals only 0.78% of sales. Other income of ₹62.71 crore exceeds PAT by a wide margin; after ₹46.87 crore depreciation and ₹26.04 crore interest, pretax profit is ₹1.26 crore. The transcript’s 4.9% EBITDA includes other income; compare operating performance using the roughly 0.8–1% excluding-other-income measure.

Price and financial dates differ: the cleaned close used here is ₹1,923.00 on 2026-11-12; the public-financial snapshot is dated 2026-11-13. The screenshot price is not treated as a live or verified valuation input. Local public-financial-data parquets, September 2026 quarter; amounts rounded to ₹ crore.

Management’s adjusted gross margin was 24%, up 1.6 points from Q1 but below 25.4% in Q4 FY26. The bridge includes 5.3 structural points,9.4 points of commodity pressure and 2.7 points of SKU benefit. Some mix gains are explicitly temporary.

business_economics: Wholesales, realized price/mix, software attachment and fixed-cost absorption drive current economics.93,000 wholesales differ from registrations and production.94% Pro attachment supports mix but does not reveal recurring software profit after development and service costs.

The gross-margin bridge starts at 25.4% in Q4 FY26, adds 5.3 structural points, subtracts 9.4 commodity points and adds 2.7 SKU-management points to reach 24%. AGM improved versus Q1 but remained below Q4, and some mix gains may reverse when supply normalizes.
earnings_quality: Local operating profit ₹11.46 cr on ₹1,464.24 cr revenue equals 0.78%. Adding ₹62.71 cr other income and subtracting ₹46.87 cr depreciation and ₹26.04 cr interest yields ₹1.26 cr pretax profit. Other income bridges most of the shortfall between operating earnings and net profitability.

The call’s 4.9% EBITDA includes other income; about 0.8–1% excluding it is the relevant operating comparison. Management warns PAT may fluctuate. Missing FY26 consolidated cash flow prevents a complete self-funding assessment.
capital_allocation: The 11.4 lakh installed-capacity target requires installation, trials, quality stabilization, utilization and retail absorption. Each is a separate capital-return milestone; more capacity also creates depreciation, working-capital and execution requirements.

The key funding question is how much cash is needed before sustainable operating cash after the AURIC ramp. Dilution, leases, debt and long warranty obligations should be included; reported investments cannot all be assumed freely distributable.
valuation_logic: Neither one positive PAT quarter nor installed capacity produces a credible P/E fair value. Revenue valuation must connect saleable vehicles to vehicle/software gross profit, normal warranty costs and cash after expansion.

A reverse model should ask what sales, utilization and sustainable EBIT margin the equity value requires, and whether funding can reach that point. Missing cash and diluted-share inputs should remain open rather than be invented.
peer_positioning: EV peers help compare retail share, service quality and battery warranties, but subsidies, development capitalization and cash needs differ. Mature incumbent P/E ratios do not translate directly to a marginally profitable expansion-stage manufacturer.

The software ecosystem may differentiate the franchise, but retention, realization and contribution after development/service costs must demonstrate that value. Attachment and search interest alone do not establish it.
